title: Operator-Authenticated Staging Proof Cockpit Access Surface
context: The staging proof cockpit is served by apps/staging-proof-cockpit/src/server.mjs. It already implements a guarded write mode (USF_PROOF_COCKPIT_ALLOW_WRITES, USF_PROOF_COCKPIT_REVIEW_SECRET, CSRF double-submit) and derives the recorded actor from a fronting authenticator identity header or from the configured USF_PROOF_COCKPIT_REVIEW_ACTOR. Until now the cockpit was run only on loopback; the public origin at 1e100.network and aldous.info served only read-only proof markers, and the operator-access gateway posture was defined-only with no operator clickthrough surface created. The accountable owner has decided the interactive cockpit is to become a permanent staging fixture at the staging FQDN /proof behind operator authentication so acceptance and signoff can be exercised in staging, and that the exposure mechanism must be clone-and-go: a composed Caddy edge served from the repository (docker/caddy/Caddyfile mounted into the external-caddy Compose service) with no host /etc/caddy file and no systemd requirement. The proof content the cockpit renders remains hermetic and synthetic; this decision changes the access surface, not the provider class of the evidence.
decision: USF permits, as a bounded staging operator proof fixture, exposure of the interactive staging proof cockpit at the staging FQDN /proof (default 1e100.network/proof). The public proof edge is a composed Caddy service external-caddy whose config is the committed docker/caddy/Caddyfile, mounted read-only into the container; there MUST be no host /etc/caddy file and no system/systemd Caddy requirement (clone-and-go). The two site addresses MUST be parameterised by env (USF_PROOF_STAGING_FQDN, USF_PROOF_PROD_FQDN) supplied as Makefile envs. The composed edge is the shared always-on public proof edge: the public read-only proof routes are served independently of any operator gate. The cockpit is realised as a profile-gated Compose service staging-proof-cockpit (profile proof-cockpit) generated for the staging Compose target, published with no host port at all and reachable only over the compose network as staging-proof-cockpit:8080. Public reachability is provided solely by the edge reverse proxy: a Caddy proof_cockpit_handlers snippet MUST be imported into the staging FQDN site only and MUST NOT be imported into the production FQDN site. The /proof gate MUST require a valid operator credential via HTTP basic authentication before proxying any /proof request and MUST preserve the established no-store and security headers. The gate MUST be a reload-managed include on a writable runtime mount whose committed default is CLOSED (responds 503, no unauthenticated fallback); the operator credential MUST live only in that runtime include, never committed and never set in the external-caddy service environment. Cockpit write actions (the single Accept, the matching Reject, and QA actions) remain gated by the cockpit write policy: served only when USF_PROOF_COCKPIT_ALLOW_WRITES is yes and a non-empty USF_PROOF_COCKPIT_REVIEW_SECRET is present, both supplied by the operator at bring-up as compose interpolation with no committed placeholder secret, and every write is CSRF-double-submit validated. The recorded actor is the configured accountable operator identity or the operator login forwarded by the edge. Acceptance is a single deliberate operator decision: one guarded Accept (POST /proof/accept) records, in one human action, an acceptance of every currently-open review item at its current evidence fingerprint and the final USF-290 human acceptance decision, and a matching Reject (POST /proof/reject) records the human-rejected decision. The single Accept is never auto-completed; it remains a deliberate human browser action requiring one confirmation checkbox in addition to the write guard and CSRF. The acceptance ledger persists to a durable Compose volume; promoting recorded acceptances into the committed evidence corpus remains a manual operator reconciliation step and MUST NOT be performed by giving the running service repository write credentials. This decision does not claim the live public deployment has been proven; that remains an operator step recorded in the runbook, and the platform non-claims are preserved.
consequences: A profile-gated staging-proof-cockpit Compose service is catalogued and generated for the staging target, with a durable acceptance-ledger volume and no host-published port (reachable only over the compose network).

The composed external-caddy edge from docker/caddy/Caddyfile becomes the shared always-on public proof origin edge with FQDN envs, a persistent caddy-data volume, and a writable runtime mount for the reload-managed /proof gate include whose committed default is CLOSED. Its gateway ports bind public 0.0.0.0:80 and 0.0.0.0:443 on the staging FQDN edge, the generated staging Compose target publishes 0.0.0.0:80 and 0.0.0.0:443 for external-caddy, and the dev/test edges remain host-portless (compose-network-only).

The operator-access-gateway posture matrix and the gateway/clickthrough substrate matrix record the accepted public proof origin edge (acceptedPublicProofOriginEdge), and the operator-access matrix records the /proof cockpit route as an active, bounded, edge-authenticated operator fixture rather than defined-only. The validate-enterprise USF-ENTERPRISE-014 and USF-ENTERPRISE-020 rules honour this narrow accepted authority for the caddy gateway ports only and continue to fail closed for every other service and for public exposure asserted without a well-formed accepted-authority block.

The human-signoff and self-hosted-origin runbooks document the composed Caddy edge, the FQDN envs, the reload-managed operator-authenticated /proof gate include, the caddy-up / proof-review-up / proof-review-down lifecycle, and the manual acceptance-record reconciliation step.
Live public deployment (DNS, TLS, applying the composed edge on a public host) remains an operator step; the platform claims no deployment, staging, or production readiness from this decision.
invariants: The public proof edge is a composed Caddy service external-caddy served from the committed docker/caddy/Caddyfile with the site FQDNs parameterised by env; there is no host /etc/caddy file and no systemd requirement.

The composed external-caddy edge is the accepted public proof origin edge: its gateway ports bind public 0.0.0.0:80 and 0.0.0.0:443 on the staging FQDN edge (hostIp 0.0.0.0, bindScope public, internetExposureAllowed true). This public bind is authorised only for the caddy gateway ports; every other service, including staging-proof-cockpit, stays loopback-only behind the edge, and LAN exposure of any operator/admin service remains denied.
The /proof cockpit route is imported only into the staging FQDN site and only behind a Caddy operator basic-authentication credential; it is never imported into the production FQDN site.

The /proof gate is a reload-managed include whose committed default is CLOSED (503); the operator credential lives only in the gitignored runtime include, never committed and never in the external-caddy service environment.

The staging-proof-cockpit Compose service publishes no host port; it is reachable only over the compose network as staging-proof-cockpit:8080, and public reachability is only via the authenticated edge reverse proxy.

Cockpit write actions are served only with USF_PROOF_COCKPIT_ALLOW_WRITES yes plus a non-empty operator-supplied review secret with no committed placeholder, and every write is CSRF-double-submit validated.

Acceptance is a single deliberate operator decision, never auto-completed: one guarded Accept (POST /proof/accept, requiring a single confirmation checkbox) records both the acceptance of every currently-open review item at its current evidence fingerprint and the final USF-290 human acceptance decision, and a matching Reject records the human-rejected decision; the machine surface never records the decision on its own.
The proof content the cockpit renders remains hermetic and synthetic; no real tenant data, real secrets, or live external provider is introduced.
The public read-only proof edge is unchanged, and all platform non-claims are preserved; the reachable operator fixture is not a platform go-live.
permittedChanges: Upgrade the edge operator authentication from basic authentication to Keycloak OIDC single sign-on via a forward-auth proxy, without changing the cockpit, once that mechanism is proven.
Generate the staging-proof-cockpit service for additional non-production environments as a compose-network-only operator fixture if a later authorised change requires it.
Add a live-deployment proof rung (DNS, TLS, origin Caddyfile apply) as a higher, separately-evidenced step without weakening the hermetic proof of the cockpit content.
forbiddenDrift: Do not expose the /proof cockpit route without the edge operator-authentication gate (the committed include default must stay CLOSED), and do not import it into the production FQDN site.

Do not bake the operator credential into the committed Caddyfile, the committed include, or the external-caddy service environment; it lives only in the gitignored runtime include. Do not reintroduce a host /etc/caddy file or a systemd Caddy for this surface.

Do not extend the public 0.0.0.0 bind beyond the two external-caddy gateway ports; the staging-proof-cockpit and every other operator/admin/control-plane service must stay loopback-only behind the edge, LAN exposure of any operator/admin service remains denied, and public reachability of any operator/admin surface is only ever via the operator-authenticated edge reverse proxy, never a direct public host port.
Do not enable cockpit write mode without a non-empty operator-supplied review secret and CSRF validation, and do not auto-complete final signoff.
Do not give the running service repository write credentials to auto-commit acceptance records into evidence.
Do not present the reachable operator fixture as staging, deployment, production, live-provider, SOC, ISO, enterprise-production, product-UI, or full-product readiness.
Do not feed real tenant data, real secrets, or live external providers into the exposed cockpit.
aiAlignmentRules: Agents must preserve the edge operator-authentication gate (reload-managed include, committed default CLOSED), the compose-network-only cockpit port (no host publish), and the staging-FQDN-only routing when changing this surface, and must keep the composed edge served from the committed docker/caddy/Caddyfile with no host /etc/caddy or systemd dependency.

Agents must preserve the cockpit write guard (allow-writes plus review secret plus CSRF) and the single deliberate, non-auto-completed operator Accept/Reject decision (one confirmation checkbox); they must not reintroduce a machine-side auto-completion of acceptance.
Agents must preserve all platform non-claims and must not relabel the reachable operator fixture as any readiness claim.
Agents must keep the cockpit rendered proof content hermetic and synthetic and must not introduce real tenant data, real secrets, or a live external provider through this surface.
rationale: The cockpit already carries the exact primitives an operator access surface needs (a fail-closed write policy, CSRF protection, and forward-auth-or-configured actor derivation), so the smallest correct change is to authenticate at a composed edge and reverse-proxy rather than build authentication into the application or weaken the write guard. Serving the edge from the committed docker/caddy/Caddyfile keeps it clone-and-go (no host /etc/caddy, no systemd), and parameterising the FQDNs by env lets the same composed edge serve staging and production sites. A reload-managed operator basic-authentication include with a committed CLOSED default keeps the operator credential out of the repository and the service environment, decouples the always-on public edge from the transient /proof gate, and is upgradeable to Keycloak OIDC single sign-on later without changing the cockpit because the cockpit already reads a forwarded identity header. Restricting the route to the staging FQDN site, keeping the cockpit reachable only over the compose network, and keeping write mode behind an operator-supplied review secret and CSRF hold the exposure to a bounded operator fixture. Preserving the platform non-claims keeps the change honest: the surface being reachable proves operator access to hermetic proof, not platform readiness, and the rendered evidence stays hermetic and synthetic, so hermetic provability is untouched.
description: Records the owner-ratified decision to expose the interactive staging proof cockpit as a permanent, bounded staging operator fixture at the staging FQDN /proof (default 1e100.network/proof), served by a composed Caddy edge (external-caddy, from the committed docker/caddy/Caddyfile with the staging and production FQDNs as Makefile envs), gated by a reload-managed operator basic-authentication include (committed default CLOSED) and reverse-proxied to a profile-gated staging-proof-cockpit Compose service reachable only over the compose network, so the accountable operator can review the current proof state and record the single deliberate Accept or Reject decision with no AI agent in the loop, while preserving every platform non-claim and the hermetic, synthetic nature of the rendered proof content.
aiGuidance: Use this ADR when evaluating exposure of the interactive staging proof cockpit at the staging FQDN /proof: the public edge is a composed Caddy service from the committed docker/caddy/Caddyfile (no host /etc/caddy, no systemd) with FQDN envs, the route is staging-FQDN-only behind a reload-managed operator basic-authentication include whose committed default is CLOSED, the staging-proof-cockpit Compose service is reachable only over the compose network with public reachability only via the authenticated edge proxy, cockpit write mode stays behind an operator-supplied review secret and CSRF with final signoff never auto-completed, the operator credential lives only in the gitignored runtime include, the rendered proof content stays hermetic and synthetic, and all platform non-claims are preserved. This is an operator access fixture, not a platform readiness claim.
